Lebaoth
leh-BAY-oth
proper noun
Hebrew Lebaoth, “lionesses,” a town in the south of Judah, called also Beth-lebaoth.

📖 Biblical Definition

Lebaoth, “lionesses,” was a town in the uttermost south of Judah, named in the catalogue of the cities given to that tribe toward the coast of Edom (Jos 15:32). It is the same place that appears among the towns of Simeon under the fuller name Beth-lebaoth, “the house of lionesses” (Jos 19:6); for the lot of Simeon fell within the inheritance of Judah, Judah’s portion being larger than that tribe could fill (Jos 19:1). Its name, drawn from the lionesses that once haunted the wild and desolate country of the Negeb, speaks of the harshness of that southern frontier, where the beasts of the field pressed close upon the settlements of God’s people. To dwell in such a land was to live in dependence upon the LORD, who keeps His people in the midst of danger and gives them rest among the lions’ dens. Lebaoth is one of the obscure towns of the south that left no further mark in the sacred history, yet it was written into the word of God among the inheritance of Simeon. It stands as a witness that the LORD plants His people even where the lionesses dwell, and keeps them by His own hand in the dry and dangerous places of the south.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A town in the south of Judah, given to Simeon as Beth-lebaoth, whose name means “lionesses.”

LEBAOTH, a town in the south of Judah (Jos 15:32).

Its name means “lionesses.”

It appears among Simeon’s towns as Beth-lebaoth (Jos 19:6).

It lay in the wild and desolate country of the Negeb.

It was written into Scripture among Simeon’s inheritance.

📖 Key Scripture

Jos 15:32 — "And Lebaoth, and Shilhim, and Ain, and Rimmon: all the cities are twenty and nine, with their villages:"

Jos 19:6 — "And Beth-lebaoth, and Sharuhen; thirteen cities and their villages:"

Jos 19:1 — "And the second lot came forth to Simeon, even for the tribe of the children of Simeon according to their families: and their inheritance was within the inheritance of the children of Judah."

Jos 19:9 — "Out of the portion of the children of Judah was the inheritance of the children of Simeon: for the part of the children of Judah was too much for them: therefore the children of Simeon had their inheritance within the inheritance of them."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A place of Scripture, not a contested doctrine; it witnesses that God keeps His people even where the lionesses dwell.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that God settled Simeon within Judah and keeps His people even in dangerous places. Lebaoth, the house of lionesses, was set in the wild country of the Negeb, where the beasts of the field pressed close upon the settlements of God’s people. To dwell in such a land was to live in dependence upon the LORD, who keeps His people in the midst of danger and gives them rest among the lions’ dens.

The fuller name Beth-lebaoth, “the house of lionesses,” under which the town appears in the lot of Simeon, witnesses the kindness of God in giving the smaller tribe a portion within the borders of the greater. Judah’s inheritance was too much for that tribe, and so the LORD made room within it for Simeon, that none of His people should be without a place. He who tames the lions of the south for His people’s sake also orders their borders, that all might dwell safely in the land He gave by lot.
